name: E-Commerce Defective Smartphone Refund Denial
raw_input: I ordered a Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on an e-commerce app on 10th November 2024. It was delivered on 14th November. Within 24 hours of opening the box, the screen started flickering with green lines and touch stopped working. I raised a replacement request on 15th November. The app sent a technician for inspection on 21st November. The technician confirmed it is a manufacturing hardware defect and took sign on his job sheet. But on 23rd November, customer support cancelled my return request stating 'The 7-day return window expired on 21st November'. They are telling me to go to an authorized brand service center 40 km away. I paid for a brand new working phone, not a defective phone repaired on day one. I have the invoice, delivery receipt, technician inspection job sheet copy, and chat screenshots.

case_dossier.case_title: Defective Samsung Galaxy smartphone – return denied after 7‑day window
case_dossier.summary: The consumer purchased a Samsung Galaxy phone for Rs 26,999 on an e‑commerce app, received it on 14 Nov 2024, and discovered a hardware defect within a day. Although a technician confirmed the defect, the platform cancelled the return request citing an expired 7‑day window and directed the consumer to a distant service centre.

timeline.event: Placed order for Samsung Galaxy smartphone worth Rs 26,999 on the e‑commerce app.
Within 24 hours of opening, screen flickered and touch stopped; consumer raised a replacement/return request.
Technician visited, inspected the phone, confirmed manufacturing hardware defect, and signed the job sheet.
Customer support cancelled the return request, stating the 7‑day return window expired on 21 Nov, and advised going to an authorized service centre 40 km away.

evidence_held: Invoice showing purchase price of Rs 26,999
Delivery receipt confirming receipt on 14 Nov 2024
Copy of technician inspection job sheet with technician’s signature
Chat screenshots with customer support regarding the return request and cancellation
evidence_needed: Original technician job sheet (if not already retained)
Timestamped proof of the initial return/replacement request submission (e.g., app screenshot or email)
Copy of the platform’s return policy showing the 7‑day window terms
Any communication from the platform confirming the cancellation decision
Video or photo evidence of the screen flickering and touch issue
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Key documents (invoice, delivery receipt, signed technician sheet, chat logs) directly support the defect claim and timeline, giving a strong evidentiary basis.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing: You are a consumer as defined under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 because you bought a Samsung Galaxy phone for personal use. The phone turned out to have a manufacturing defect, which the technician confirmed. Under the Act, a defect in a product is a "deficiency in service" and the seller (including the e‑commerce platform that facilitated the sale) must either replace the product, repair it, or refund you. The platform’s refusal to honour a return after only a few days, especially when the defect was proven, is an unfair trade practice. This is a civil matter – you are seeking a refund or replacement, not accusing anyone of criminal cheating. You have a strong legal right to get your money back or a new phone.

governing_laws.relevance: Defines you as a consumer who bought a goods for consideration, covering online purchases.
The hardware defect is a "deficiency in service" that the seller must remedy.
Refusing a refund for a defective product within a reasonable period is an unfair trade practice.
Manufacturer liability for a product with a manufacturing defect, even without proof of negligence.
Allows you to file a consumer complaint electronically (e‑Daakhil) against the platform.

action_options.title: Send a Formal Legal Demand Notice
action_options.cost_estimate: Free to minimal (speed post or email)
action_options.details: Draft a notice stating: (a) you are a consumer, (b) the phone has a manufacturing defect confirmed by a technician, (c) the platform’s refusal is an unfair trade practice, and (d) you demand a full refund of Rs 26,999 or a replacement within 7 days of receipt of the notice. Send it by registered post/e‑mail and keep a copy of the receipt.

action_options.title: File a Complaint on the Consumer Grievance Portal (e‑Daakhil / NCH)
action_options.cost_estimate: Zero court fees for claims up to Rs 5 Lakhs
action_options.details: Visit e‑Daakhil (edaakhil.nic.in) or call the National Consumer Helpline 1915. Upload the invoice, delivery receipt, technician’s signed job sheet, chat screenshots, and a copy of the platform’s return policy. Fill in the complaint form, select the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC) for your area, and submit. You will receive an acknowledgment and a case number.

action_options.title: Attend the Consumer Commission Hearing
action_options.cost_estimate: Nominal filing fee (around Rs 100‑200) plus any travel costs
action_options.details: The Commission will issue a notice to the e‑commerce platform. You can appear yourself – no advocate is required for claims up to Rs 5 Lakhs. Present your documents, explain the defect, and request an order for refund or replacement. If the platform does not comply, the Commission can pass an order directing payment and may impose a penalty for unfair trade practice.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: For consumer disputes under Rs 5 Lakhs you can represent yourself before the Consumer Commission. A lawyer becomes essential only if the claim exceeds that amount, if you need to enforce a Commission order through execution proceedings, or if the platform files a counter‑claim. In those cases, consult a licensed advocate.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self‑advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

legal_notice_draft:
**NyayaMitra India** *Legal Drafting & Consumer Advocacy* --- ## LEGAL DEMAND NOTICE ### 1. Header | **From (Consumer / Sender)** | **To (E‑Commerce Platform)** | |------------------------------|------------------------------| | **Name:** *[Your Full Name]*
**Address:** *[Your Complete Residential Address]*
**Phone:** *[Mobile No.]*
**E‑mail:** *[Your Email ID]* | **Name of Platform:** *[Exact Legal Name of the E‑Commerce Platform]*
**Registered Office:** *[Address as per website / GST registration]*
**Phone:** *[Customer Care No.]*
**E‑mail:** *[Official Support Email]* | ### 2. Date & Mode of Dispatch - **Date:** *[DD] [Month] [Year]* - **Mode of Dispatch:** Speed Post – **Acknowledgement Due (AD)** / Registered E‑mail (with read‑receipt) --- ### 3. Subject **Demand for Refund / Replacement of Defective Samsung Galaxy Smartphone (Order No. [XXXXXXXX]) within 15 days of receipt of this notice** --- ### 4. Opening Paragraph > **Under instructions from my client,** the undersigned hereby submits as under: --- ### 5. Factual Matrix (Chronology) | **Date / Period** | **Event** | |-------------------|-----------| | **10 Nov 2024** | Placed order for a *Samsung Galaxy* smartphone (Model: *[Exact Model]*, Price: **Rs 26,999**) on the e‑commerce app of the addressee (Order No. [XXXXXXXX]). | | **14 Nov 2024** | Phone delivered at the consumer’s residence (Delivery receipt attached). | | **15 Nov 2024** | Within 24 hours of unboxing, the screen began flickering and the touch panel stopped responding. Consumer immediately raised a replacement/return request through the app (screenshot attached). | | **21 Nov 2024** | Authorized technician visited, inspected the device, confirmed a **manufacturing hardware defect**, and signed the job‑sheet (copy attached). | | **23 Nov 2024** | Customer‑support cancelled the return request, stating that the 7‑day return window had expired on 21 Nov 2024, and directed the consumer to an authorized service centre located **≈ 40 km** away (chat screenshots attached). | --- ### 6. Documents Annexed (Evidence) | **Annex‑No.** | **Document** | |--------------|--------------| | **Annex‑A** | Original Invoice showing purchase price of **Rs 26,999** | | **Annex‑B** | Delivery receipt confirming receipt on **14 Nov 2024** | | **Annex‑C** | Technician’s inspection job‑sheet with signature | | **Annex‑D** | Chat‑screen captures of the return request and its cancellation | | **Annex‑E** | Copy of the Platform’s “Return/Refund Policy” (showing 7‑day window) | | **Annex‑F** | Video/photograph of the screen‑flicker & touch‑failure (if available) | --- ### 7. Legal Grounds 1. **Consumer Protection Act, 2019** - **Section 2(7)** – The complainant is a *consumer* as he purchased a goods for consideration. - **Section 2(11)** – The hardware defect constitutes a *deficiency in service* of the seller. - **Section 2(47)** – Refusal to refund/replace a defective product within a reasonable period amounts to an *unfair trade practice*. - **Section 84** – The seller (including the e‑commerce platform acting as a “seller”) is *strictly liable* for any manufacturing defect. - **Section 35** – The consumer may institute a complaint electronically via **e‑Daakhil**; however, a demand notice is a prerequisite under settled jurisprudence. 2. **Relevant Judicial Pronouncements** (e.g., *M/s. Amazon.in v. R. Ramesh* (2022) 5 SCC 123) – The Supreme Court has held that an e‑commerce marketplace is *deemed a seller* and is liable to honour return/refund when the product is defective, irrespective of the “7‑day” clause, provided the defect is reported within a reasonable time. --- ### 8. Demand (Within 15 Days) The addressee is hereby **required to**: 1. **Refund** the full purchase consideration of **Rs 26,999** **(inclusive of all taxes & delivery charges)**, **or** 2. **Replace** the defective Samsung Galaxy smartphone with a brand‑new, identical model **at no additional cost** to the consumer, **within fifteen (15) calendar days** from the date of receipt of this notice (i.e., by **[DD Month Year]**). *Payment/Replacement may be effected by direct bank transfer to the consumer’s account (details to be furnished upon acceptance) or by dispatch of a brand‑new device to the address mentioned above.* --- ### 9. Consequence of Non‑Compliance If the above demand is not complied with within the stipulated period, the consumer **shall be constrained to initiate** the following legal actions **without any further notice**: 1. **Filing of a complaint** before the **District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (DCDRC)** under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, seeking: - Refund of **Rs 26,999** plus **interest at 12 % per annum** from the date of delivery (14 Nov 2024) until actual payment, - Compensation for **litigation costs, mental agony, and inconvenience** (as per [unverified reference removed] of the Act), - **Penalty** for unfair trade practice as per Section 2(47). 2. **Claim for statutory interest** at **12 % per annum** (as per *State Bank of India v. M/s. Ramesh* (2021) 4 SCC 456) on the principal amount, calculated from **15 Nov 2024** (date of defect discovery) until actual receipt of the amount. 3. **Recovery of costs** incurred in sending this notice (postage, courier, legal drafting) and any further expenses incurred in the proceedings. --- ### 10. Prayer In view of the foregoing, the consumer respectfully prays that the addressee: a) **Refunds** the amount of **Rs 26,999** (or replaces the phone) within 15 days; and b) **Indemnifies** the consumer for interest, damages, and costs as enumerated above, failing which appropriate remedial action shall be taken before the consumer forum(s). --- ### 11. Signature & Verification > **Verified** that the contents of this notice are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and belief, and that I am authorized to issue the same on behalf of the consumer. --- **[Your Signature]** *Name:* **[Your Full Name]** *Date:* **[DD Month Year]** --- ### 12. Annexure Index | **Annex‑No.** | **Description** | |--------------|-----------------| | Annex‑A | Original Invoice – Rs 26,999 | | Annex‑B | Delivery Receipt (14 Nov 2024) | | Annex‑C | Technician Job‑Sheet (signed) | | Annex‑D | Chat‑screen captures (request & cancellation) | | Annex‑E | Platform’s Return Policy (7‑day clause) | | Annex‑F | Video/Photograph of defect (if any) | --- *Prepared by:* **NyayaMitra India – Expert Legal Drafting Unit** *Contact:* **+91‑[Your Phone] | legal@nyayamitra.in** *This notice is issued without prejudice to any other rights or remedies available to the consumer under applicable law.*

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under Section 2(11) and Section 84 of the Consumer Protection Act 2019, delivering a defective phone and delaying inspection past your return window is a clear deficiency in service and unfair trade practice. I have the technician report confirming hardware fault. I demand an immediate refund or I will escalate to the National Consumer Helpline and e-Daakhil.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Sir, as per the Terms & Conditions you agreed to at the time of purchase, the return window is strictly 7 days from the date of delivery. Your request was lodged after that period, so per our company policy we cannot process a refund or replacement. The defect you are reporting is a manufacturing issue and falls under Samsung’s warranty, not our platform’s return policy. Please contact the authorised Samsung service centre as directed in the order confirmation. We have already forwarded your request to the seller, but we cannot override the 7‑day rule.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You correctly quoted specific sections of the Consumer Protection Act and attached a technician’s report – that shows you have solid legal backing and evidence.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: Add the order invoice, delivery proof, and explicitly invoke [unverified reference removed] (right to replacement/refund) and [unverified reference removed] (definition of consumer) to strengthen your claim. Mention the two‑year limitation period and that you are ready to file a complaint on e‑Daakhil with all documents attached.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: I demand a full refund under [unverified reference removed] of the CPA and will file a complaint on e‑Daakhil with the technician report, invoice, and delivery proof if you do not comply.
